trial_court: High Court of Judicature at Patna, C.R. No.876 of 2007
facts_of_case: Petitioner's prayer for deciding the application filed under section 24 of Hindu Marriages Act was sought to be deferred by the trial court. The petitioner had been seeking maintenance since 6.9.2001 but no order was passed till date.

legal_principles.principle: The object of section 24 of the Hindu Marriages Act is to provide immediate relief.
legal_principles.held: This Court would find some substance in the aforementioned submission of the counsel for the petitioner. The whole object of section 24 of the Hindu Marriages Act is to provide immediate relief and in fact the time limit fixed under section 24 for passing an order of adinterim maintenance is only 60 days.

legal_principles.principle: An allegation of adultery cannot be a ground for refusal of maintenance in terms of Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: Added to it even an allegation of petitioner living in adultery, unless proved in course of the matrimonial case cannot be a ground for refusal of amount of maintenance in terms of Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

outcome.final_order: The court below is directed to pass a final order under section 24 of the Hindu Marriages Act within one month from the date of receipt/production of a copy of this order and payment of any amount that may be fixed by the court.

keywords: Latin maxim: justice delayed is justice denied
use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage Act applications
